Example 2.4.2.2: ML and REML estimates of variance components

Source: R/examples.R
Examp2.4.2.2.Rd

The split-plot data ex125: REML gives 5.151 (region), 0.387 (herd within region) and 2.096 (residual); ML gives the smaller 4.292, 0.322 and 1.747 (Table 2.4.2.1), because it ignores the degrees of freedom used by the fixed effects. The Type 3 (moment) estimates equal REML here, as the data are balanced.

References

Duchateau, L., Janssen, P. and Rowlands, G. J. (1998). Linear Mixed Models. An Introduction with Applications in Veterinary Research. International Livestock Research Institute, Nairobi.

See also

vlm_fit, ex125

Other VetResearchLMM examples: Examp1.3.2, Examp2.2.1.7, Examp2.3.2, Examp2.4.3.1, Examp2.5.1.1, Examp2.5.2.1, Examp2.5.3.1, Examp2.5.4.1, Examp2.6.1, Examp3.1, Examp3.2, Examp3.3

Examples

# SAS program of the book (Appendix B):
#   proc mixed data=ex125 method=ml;   * and method=reml;
#     class drug dose region;
#     model pcv = drug dose drug*dose;
#     random region drug*region;
#   run;

ml <-
  vlm_fit(
      fixed    = Pcv ~ Drug + dose + Drug:dose
    , data     = ex125
    , random   = ~ Region + Region:Drug
    , repeated = NULL
    , method   = "ML"
    , ddfm     = "default"
    , type     = 3
    , class    = NULL
    , bound    = TRUE
    , control  = list()
    )
reml <-
  vlm_fit(
      fixed    = Pcv ~ Drug + dose + Drug:dose
    , data     = ex125
    , random   = ~ Region + Region:Drug
    , repeated = NULL
    , method   = "REML"
    , ddfm     = "default"
    , type     = 3
    , class    = NULL
    , bound    = TRUE
    , control  = list()
    )
mom <-
  vlm_fit(
      fixed    = Pcv ~ Drug + dose + Drug:dose
    , data     = ex125
    , random   = ~ Region + Region:Drug
    , repeated = NULL
    , method   = "Type3"
    , ddfm     = "default"
    , type     = 3
    , class    = NULL
    , bound    = TRUE
    , control  = list()
    )
cbind(ML = ml$covariance$estimate, REML = reml$covariance$estimate, Type3 = mom$covariance$estimate)
#>            ML     REML    Type3
#> [1,] 4.292361 5.150833 5.150833
#> [2,] 0.322500 0.387000 0.387000
#> [3,] 1.747014 2.096417 2.096417

# the same model with lme4 (optional)
if (requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE)) {
  lm4 <-
    lme4::lmer(
        formula = Pcv ~ Drug * dose + (1 | Region / Drug)
      , data    = ex125
      , REML    = TRUE
      )
  print(lme4::VarCorr(lm4), comp = "Variance")
}
#>  Groups      Name        Variance
#>  Drug:Region (Intercept) 0.3870  
#>  Region      (Intercept) 5.1508  
#>  Residual                2.0964
